front.title: Code Generation from the Concise Data Definition Language (CDDL): Authoring Guidance and Open Questions

abstract.t:
The Concise Data Definition Language (CDDL) was specified to express the structure of CBOR and JSON data, principally so that instances can be validated against a specification. It is now starting to be used as the source from which encoders and decoders are generated.
Compilation exercises a specification language in ways that validation does not. This document records three things. First, guidance for CDDL authors on which constructions compile to small, fast, one-pass code and which do not. Second, a description of what a code generator has to do with a CDDL specification, and where implementation and run-time cost lies. Third, a set of questions where RFC 8610 and its updates say nothing, are under-determined, or determine in a way that deployed specifications do not follow, each with a motivating example drawn where possible from a published RFC or an active Internet-Draft.
This document is a discussion input. It creates no requirements on implementations and defines no new CDDL syntax.
